interface.name: gyro_bindings_v1

description.summary: keys the shell claims before any window sees them

interface.description:
A shell declares the chords it answers to, once, and is told when one is pressed. This is the seam that lets a shell open a launcher, an overview or a switcher without gyro knowing what any of those are.
A key that matches a declared chord does not reach the surface that has the keyboard. The compositor's own keys are matched first and cannot be claimed here: gyro is a boot service holding the display with no virtual terminal behind it, and the way out of it may not be something a client can take.
A chord is a keysym and a set of modifiers rather than a keycode, so that a shell configured with the key a person sees printed on the key gets that key under every layout. The keysym is the one the key produces at the first shift level of the layout in effect, so a chord is written the way a person would say it aloud - "super and space" - rather than as whatever character the modifiers would have produced.
This is not a general shortcut service. Every object here belongs to a client the compositor has granted the run of a session, and an application is never offered this global.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Bindings already created are unaffected and go on being delivered until they are destroyed themselves.

request.name: claim
request.description:
Claims a chord and creates the object its presses arrive on.
Modifiers not named must not be held for the chord to match, so "super and space" does not fire when control is also down. Modifiers that are not one of the four - a lock, a layout switch - are not consulted at all.
The same chord may be claimed more than once, by this client or another, and every binding that matches is told. There is no ownership of a key here and so no request that can fail because somebody else asked first: a session with both a shell and a screen recorder in it is an ordinary one, and refusing the second is a refusal the second party can do nothing about.
A keysym that no key on the layout produces is accepted and never fires. The layout is the compositor's to choose and may change under a binding that was correct when it was made, so this cannot be an error.

arg.name: modifiers
arg.summary: the modifiers that must be held

arg.name: keysym
arg.summary: the XKB keysym of the key itself

enum.name: modifier

description.summary: the modifiers a chord can be written in terms of

enum.description: The four modifiers a person names when describing a shortcut. There is deliberately no entry for a lock or for a layout group: a shortcut that stopped working because caps lock was on would be one nobody could diagnose.

interface.name: gyro_binding_v1
interface.description: A chord that has been claimed, and the object its presses arrive on. It goes on delivering until the client destroys it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Releases the chord. The key reaches whatever has the keyboard from the next press onward.

event.name: pressed
event.description:
The chord was pressed. The key did not reach the surface holding the keyboard and no release will be sent for it either.
The timestamp is the instant the key transition was reported by the input device, on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, and it is the point of this event rather than a detail of it. It is the origin an animation the shell starts should be stamped with: two clients reacting to the same press name the same instant, so the compositor composes what they commit into one gesture, and a commit that arrives a frame late renders already in progress by exactly the right amount rather than starting from nothing. A shell that stamped its own handling time instead would produce a launcher that opens a little later on a busy machine, which is the variability this whole design exists to remove.
It is sent at nanosecond resolution rather than the truncated milliseconds wl_keyboard.key carries, for the same reason: a millisecond is a fifteenth of a frame at 60Hz and a fortieth at 165Hz, and rounding the origin is rounding where the animation starts.
There is no released event. A chord that a person holds - a switcher walked with a modifier down - needs one and needs the modifier releases that go with it, and neither is specified here yet.

arg.name: tv_sec_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp

arg.name: tv_sec_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the seconds part of the timestamp
